thesis: Partial information can support disciplined reasoning when possibility, necessity, approximation and relational dependence remain explicit.

ideas.statement: Possibility requires one compatible world; entailment requires all; incompatible premises must be reported rather than treated as every answer succeeding.
Refinement narrows possibilities, while revision can restore possibilities after a false premise is withdrawn; provenance enables retraction.
Fixed points indicate closure under available propagators, not complete solutions; termination relies on finite monotone fair refinement or lossy widening.
Sound overapproximation preserves actual possibilities but may admit spurious ones; exact compositional summaries require stronger compatibility.
Relations among frontier values can carry decisive information that individual descriptions lose; compact algebra may preserve it without enumeration.
Vector size or symbol length alone hides interpreter, retrieval and interference costs.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Parity suffices for addition parity but not size comparisons.
Knowing y equals x makes their difference zero; independent intervals forget this.
Binary equality constraints can expose a contradiction through linear elimination instead of all assignments.
Unknown values can be represented as sets narrowed by constraints without prematurely selecting one value.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: A maximally broad sound description can be useless; measure discrimination and false alarms.
Interfaces may themselves grow rapidly and require different algebras for different domains.

audit.notes: Read every unit; preserve proposed versus demonstrated status.
